newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico seeks to boost mining output in '97.
newsitem.headline: Mexico seeks to boost mining output in '97.

text.p: The Mexican government hopes to boost mining output in 1997 through promoting credits to smaller companies and continuing exploratory studies of mining potential, the trade ministry said on Monday.
"There still persist limitations to improving efficiency and productivity that help to substitute imports, especially all non-metallic minerals," the ministry said in a year-end report.
The ministry said the mining industry lacked money and support from the private sector to study mineral reserve levels.
In response, the government established a fund it said freed up credit for small and medium-sized businesses.

In the past two years the government said it conducted 28 studies of mining potential in central Mexican states. States have also tendered exploration contracts for mineral-rich zones in the past year.

National and foreign mining companies are expected to invest $5.92 billion in Mexico over the next five years, the trade ministry has said. The ministry said bank loans to mining companies from a government-established trust totalled 1.2 billion pesos in the past two years. The trust has also given credits to state governments to buy mining equipment, the ministry said. -- Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7903
